title: System design
idea: System design is choosing how servers, databases and queues fit together. A good design keeps a backend fast and running as users and data grow.
points: A bottleneck is the part that limits everything else; each design step removes one.
Every step adds new parts to run and new ways to fail.
Start simple, and change the design only when a measured limit forces it.
This chapter walks the journey from one server to many services, step by step.

items.label: One server
items.text: App and database share one machine. Simple, and enough to start.

items.label: A bigger machine
items.text: Vertical scaling: more CPU and memory on the same server.

items.label: More machines
items.text: Horizontal scaling: several servers behind a load balancer.

items.label: Scale the database
items.text: Read replicas for reads; shards when data outgrows one machine.

items.label: Split the app
items.text: Separate services that talk through APIs, queues and events.

pitfalls: Do not copy a large company's architecture for a small app.
Do not add moving parts you cannot monitor; their failures stay invisible.

quiz.q: Pages load slowly for your users. What is the best first step?
quiz.why: A fix only helps if it targets the real limit. Measure first, then pick the step that removes that limit.

takeaway: Add complexity only when a measured bottleneck demands it.
